problem: Word won't open
description: The user double-clicks Microsoft Word or a Word document, but the program never opens, shows no window, or shows an error before it can fully load.
symptoms: Nothing happens when clicking the Word icon
A brief loading cursor appears then disappears with no window opening
Error message appears before Word finishes loading
Word may appear briefly in Task Manager processes but no window shows
possible_causes: A corrupted Word template file (Normal.dotm)
A problematic add-in loading at startup
A corrupted Office installation
Conflicting antivirus software blocking Word from launching
Insufficient system resources or a stuck background process
Windows needs updates for compatibility
diagnostic_questions: Does this happen every time, or only sometimes?
Do other Office programs like Excel open normally?
Did this start after installing an add-in, update, or new software?
Does Word appear in Task Manager as a running process even though no window shows?

commands.purpose: Open Word in Safe Mode, which disables add-ins and templates, to see if it opens without them
commands.expected_result: Word opens successfully in Safe Mode
commands.abnormal_result: Word still fails to open even in Safe Mode, pointing to a deeper installation problem

commands.purpose: Force close any stuck Word process that might be preventing a new window from opening
commands.expected_result: Process ends successfully, allowing a fresh attempt to open Word
commands.abnormal_result: Error saying the process was not found, meaning Word was not actually running in the background

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check Task Manager to see if Word is already running as a hidden or stuck process
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Sometimes a previous Word session is stuck in the background, blocking a new window from appearing

troubleshooting_steps.action: End any stuck winword.exe process in Task Manager and try opening Word again
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This clears a frozen background instance that could be silently blocking new windows

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try opening Word in Safe Mode using winword /safe from the Run box
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This disables add-ins and custom templates, helping identify if one of them is preventing normal startup

troubleshooting_steps.action: If Safe Mode works, disable recently added add-ins from File > Options > Add-ins
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This isolates and removes the specific add-in causing Word to fail to open normally

troubleshooting_steps.action: Rename the Normal.dotm template file found in the Word startup folder, allowing Word to create a fresh one
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A corrupted default template is a common cause of Word failing to open

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run the Office Quick Repair tool from Control Panel > Programs > Microsoft Office > Change
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This automatically fixes many common causes of Office programs failing to launch

troubleshooting_steps.action: Temporarily disable antivirus software to test if it is blocking Word from launching
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some antivirus programs mistakenly block Office applications from starting

troubleshooting_steps.action: If Quick Repair does not help, run Online Repair, which reinstalls Office components
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This resolves deeper corruption that a quick repair cannot fix

possible_solutions: End a stuck Word process in Task Manager
Disable a problematic add-in
Rename or reset the Normal.dotm template
Run Office Quick Repair or Online Repair
Temporarily disable antivirus software to test
Reinstall Microsoft Office completely as a last resort
prevention: Only install trusted, necessary Word add-ins
Keep Office updated regularly
Avoid force-closing Word improperly, which can corrupt templates
Keep antivirus software properly configured to avoid false blocks

problem: Word is not responding
description: While the user is working in Word, the program suddenly freezes, the window title shows 'Not Responding', and no clicks or keyboard input have any effect.
symptoms: Window title bar shows 'Word (Not Responding)'
Screen may appear greyed out or frozen
Cannot type, click, or scroll within the document
May happen during typing, saving, or opening a large document
possible_causes: A large or complex document with many images, tables, or tracked changes
A problematic add-in causing the freeze
Auto-save or auto-recovery trying to save at the same moment as another action
Insufficient system memory
A corrupted document
A printer driver issue if the freeze happens near a print action
diagnostic_questions: Does this happen with all documents, or one specific document?
Is the document unusually large or does it contain many images or tracked changes?
Does this happen at a specific moment, such as while saving, printing, or typing?
How long does the freeze typically last before recovering or needing to be closed?

commands.purpose: Check if Word is truly frozen or just working slowly, and monitor its CPU and memory usage
commands.expected_result: Word shows normal resource usage, or 'Not Responding' with high usage indicating heavy processing
commands.abnormal_result: Word shows 0% CPU usage while frozen for a long time, suggesting it is stuck rather than just working slowly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Wait a minute or two before assuming Word is completely frozen, especially with a large document
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Word can appear unresponsive briefly while processing large amounts of data, such as during auto-save

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check Task Manager to see Word's CPU usage while it appears frozen
troubleshooting_steps.reason: High usage suggests Word is still working, while 0% usage over time suggests it is truly stuck

troubleshooting_steps.action: If Word recovers, save the document immediately using Save As to create a fresh copy
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This protects the user's work in case the freeze happens again or the file has begun to show early signs of corruption

troubleshooting_steps.action: If Word does not recover after several minutes, close it through Task Manager and reopen it, checking if Word offers to recover unsaved changes
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Word's AutoRecover feature can often restore most of the recent work after a forced closure

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the freezing happens consistently with one specific document versus all documents
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is with Word generally or a specific corrupted or overly complex document

troubleshooting_steps.action: Disable recently added add-ins through File > Options > Add-ins
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Add-ins are a common cause of unpredictable freezing during normal use

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the document is very large or has extensive tracked changes, try accepting or removing old tracked changes and comments to reduce complexity
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Large amounts of tracked changes and comments can significantly slow down Word's performance

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run Office Quick Repair if the freezing continues across multiple documents
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This can fix underlying installation issues contributing to general instability

possible_solutions: Wait for large documents to finish processing
Save work using Save As once recovered
Recover unsaved changes using AutoRecover after a forced close
Disable a problematic add-in
Reduce document complexity by cleaning up tracked changes
Run Office Quick Repair
prevention: Save documents frequently while working
Keep documents to a reasonable size and complexity when possible
Only use necessary, trusted add-ins
Keep Office updated

problem: Word document is corrupted and will not open properly
description: The user tries to open a Word document, but receives an error message saying the file is corrupted or unreadable, or the document opens showing garbled text and symbols instead of the normal content.
symptoms: Error message such as 'Word found unreadable content'
Message asking if the user wants Word to try to recover the document
Document opens but shows strange characters or missing formatting
File will not open at all, showing a generic error
possible_causes: The file was not saved completely due to a crash or power loss
The file was copied or transferred incorrectly, causing data corruption
A virus or malware damaged the file
The storage device (USB drive, network drive) had an error while saving
The file extension does not match the actual file format
diagnostic_questions: Did the computer crash, lose power, or close unexpectedly while this document was open or being saved?
Where is the file stored, such as locally, on a USB drive, or a network location?
Was this file copied, emailed, or transferred from another location recently?
Do you have a recent backup or an earlier saved version of this document?

troubleshooting_steps.action: When Word shows a recovery prompt, choose to let it try to open and repair the document
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Word has a built-in repair feature that can often recover most of the content from a corrupted file automatically

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the automatic prompt does not appear, open Word first, then use File > Open, select the file, and choose 'Open and Repair' from the dropdown next to the Open button
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This manually triggers the same repair process for files that do not prompt automatically

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the AutoRecover folder for a recent automatically saved version of the document
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Word periodically saves recovery copies that may be more recent or less damaged than the main corrupted file

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if a backup copy exists, such as in a cloud storage version history, a previous email attachment, or a USB backup
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A backup copy avoids the need for repair entirely and guarantees complete, undamaged content

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try opening the file on a different computer or using a different program that can read Word documents
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the corruption is truly in the file itself, or related to a problem with this specific computer's Word installation

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the document contains recoverable text but has lost formatting, try opening it as plain text or using the 'Recover Text from Any File' option in Word's Open dialog
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This extracts at least the raw text content even when full formatting recovery is not possible

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a malware scan if corruption happened without any clear explanation like a crash or transfer error
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Unexplained file corruption can sometimes be caused by malware damaging files on the system

possible_solutions: Use Word's 'Open and Repair' feature
Recover a version from the AutoRecover folder
Restore from a cloud or manual backup
Extract raw text using 'Recover Text from Any File'
Open the file on a different computer or program to test
Remove malware if it may have caused the corruption
prevention: Save documents frequently while working
Use cloud storage with version history for important documents
Use a UPS to avoid power loss during saving
Safely eject USB drives before removing them
Keep antivirus software active and updated

problem: Cannot save a Word document
description: The user tries to save a Word document, but receives an error message, the save button appears to do nothing, or the document will not save to the intended location.
symptoms: Error message such as 'Word cannot save this file due to a naming conflict, or another error'
Save appears to complete but no changes are actually saved
Error mentioning permission or access denied
Saving to a specific location fails while saving elsewhere works
possible_causes: The file is set to read-only
Insufficient permissions to save to the chosen folder or network location
The destination drive or folder is full or disconnected
The file name contains characters not allowed in file names
A network connection was lost while saving to a network location
The document is open and locked by another user (in a shared environment)
diagnostic_questions: What exact error message appears when trying to save?
Where are you trying to save the file, such as locally, on a USB drive, or a network/shared location?
Does saving with a different file name or in a different location work?
Is this file shared with or currently open by another person?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Read the exact error message shown when the save fails
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The specific wording often points directly to the cause, such as a permissions or naming issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try saving the document with File > Save As to a different location, such as the Desktop
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is with the specific destination or the document itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the file is marked as read-only by right-clicking the file in File Explorer, checking Properties, and unchecking Read-only if selected
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A read-only file cannot be saved over until this attribute is removed

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check available storage space on the destination drive
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A completely full drive will prevent any new save operations from completing

troubleshooting_steps.action: If saving to a network or shared drive, confirm the network connection is currently working
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A dropped network connection during saving is a common cause of save failures in shared environments

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the file name contains special characters that are not allowed, such as / \ : * ? " < > |
troubleshooting_steps.reason: These characters are restricted in file names and will cause save errors if used

troubleshooting_steps.action: If working in a shared environment, check if someone else has the file open, which can lock it from being saved by others
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Simultaneous access without proper co-authoring features can cause save conflicts

troubleshooting_steps.action: As a safety measure, copy all the document text into a new blank document and save that instead if the original file consistently fails to save
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This preserves the user's work using a completely fresh file, bypassing whatever specific issue affects the original

possible_solutions: Remove the read-only attribute from the file
Save to a different location to confirm the file works
Free up space on the destination drive
Fix or wait for the network connection to a shared drive
Rename the file to remove invalid characters
Save content into a new document if the original remains broken
prevention: Regularly check available storage space
Avoid special characters in file names
Use a stable network connection when saving to shared drives
Coordinate with others when working on shared documents

problem: Cannot print from Word
description: The user tries to print a Word document, but nothing happens, an error message appears, or the printed page comes out blank or incorrect.
symptoms: Print command in Word appears to do nothing
Error message when trying to print
Print job appears in the printer queue but never prints
Printed page is blank or shows incorrect formatting
possible_causes: The printer is offline, out of paper, or has another physical issue
The wrong printer is selected in the print settings
The print spooler service has stopped
An outdated or corrupted printer driver
The document has a formatting or compatibility issue with the specific printer
A stuck print job blocking new print jobs from starting
diagnostic_questions: Can you print a test page or a document from another program, like Notepad?
Is the correct printer selected in the print dialog?
Does the printer show as online and ready?
Does an error message appear, or does nothing happen at all when printing?

commands.purpose: Check if the Print Spooler service is running
commands.abnormal_result: Service is stopped, which prevents all printing until it is restarted

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try printing a simple test document from another program, such as Notepad
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This determines if the problem is specific to Word or affects printing across the whole computer

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the correct printer is selected in Word's print dialog before printing
troubleshooting_steps.reason: It is common to accidentally have a different printer, such as a 'Print to PDF' option, selected instead of the intended physical printer

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the printer itself for basic issues, such as being powered on, connected, having paper, and not showing an error on its display
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Physical printer issues are one of the most common and simplest causes of failed print jobs

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the print queue for stuck jobs and cancel any that are stuck, then try printing again
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A stuck job can block all new print jobs from processing until it is cleared

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the Print Spooler service using services.msc
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This service manages all print jobs, and restarting it can clear many temporary printing problems

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update or reinstall the printer driver
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An outdated or corrupted driver can cause print jobs to fail specifically or inconsistently

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try printing the document as a PDF first, then print the PDF, to see if the problem is specific to Word's printing process
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps isolate whether the issue is with Word itself or the printer and driver setup

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the document has unusual formatting, very large images, or an unusual page size that could be causing a compatibility issue with the printer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some complex or unusually formatted documents can cause specific printers to fail or produce blank pages

possible_solutions: Select the correct printer before printing
Fix physical printer issues like paper or connection problems
Clear stuck print jobs from the queue
Restart the Print Spooler service
Update or reinstall the printer driver
Print as PDF first to isolate the cause
prevention: Keep printer drivers updated
Regularly clear old stuck print jobs
Check printer status before large print jobs
Confirm the correct printer is set as default

problem: AutoSave is not working in Word
description: The user expects Word to automatically save their document periodically, especially when using OneDrive or SharePoint, but changes are not being saved automatically, risking lost work if Word closes unexpectedly.
symptoms: The AutoSave toggle at the top of the Word window is turned off or greyed out
Changes made are not reflected when reopening the document after a crash
AutoRecover files are missing or outdated after an unexpected closure
Document is not saved to OneDrive or SharePoint as expected
possible_causes: The document is saved locally rather than to OneDrive or SharePoint, where AutoSave requires cloud storage
AutoSave is manually turned off in Word settings
The user is not signed in to their Microsoft account
Internet connection issues preventing sync to OneDrive or SharePoint
AutoRecover settings (a separate feature from AutoSave) have a long save interval or are disabled
diagnostic_questions: Is the document currently saved to OneDrive or SharePoint, or is it saved only locally on the computer?
Are you signed in to your Microsoft account within Word?
Is the AutoSave toggle at the top of the Word window turned on or off?
Do you have a stable internet connection available right now?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the document is saved to OneDrive or SharePoint, since AutoSave only works with files stored in these cloud locations
troubleshooting_steps.reason: AutoSave is specifically a cloud-based feature and does not work for files saved only to a local hard drive

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the document is local, use File > Save As and choose the OneDrive location to move it to the cloud
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This enables AutoSave to function, since it requires the file to be stored in a supported cloud location

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the AutoSave toggle switch at the top left of the Word window, next to the Save icon, and turn it on if it is off
troubleshooting_steps.reason: AutoSave can be manually turned off, and this is the most direct way to check and correct its status

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm you are signed in to the correct Microsoft account within Word, checking the account status in the top right corner
troubleshooting_steps.reason: AutoSave to OneDrive or SharePoint requires being properly signed in to the associated account

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check that the computer has a stable internet connection, since AutoSave needs to upload changes continuously
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Without internet access, AutoSave cannot function even if the file is technically stored in a cloud location

troubleshooting_steps.action: For extra protection regardless of AutoSave, check that Word's separate AutoRecover feature is enabled with a reasonably short save interval, found under File > Options > Save
troubleshooting_steps.reason: AutoRecover works independently of AutoSave and provides a safety net for local files by periodically saving recovery copies

troubleshooting_steps.action: Manually save the document frequently using Ctrl+S as a reliable habit, regardless of AutoSave status
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This ensures work is not lost even if AutoSave or AutoRecover encounters an unexpected problem

possible_solutions: Move the document to OneDrive or SharePoint to enable AutoSave
Turn on the AutoSave toggle manually
Sign in to the correct Microsoft account in Word
Ensure a stable internet connection is available
Enable and shorten the AutoRecover save interval for local files
Save manually and frequently as a backup habit
prevention: Store important documents in OneDrive or SharePoint
Stay signed in to the correct Microsoft account
Keep AutoRecover enabled with a short save interval
Build a habit of saving manually with Ctrl+S regularly

problem: Spell check is not working in Word
description: The user notices that Word is not underlining misspelled words with the usual red squiggly line, or the spell check tool reports no errors even in text that clearly contains mistakes.
symptoms: No red squiggly lines appear under misspelled words
Running Spelling & Grammar check manually reports no issues, even in text with obvious errors
Spell check may work in some documents but not others
Grammar check (blue or green underlines) may also be affected
possible_causes: Spell check is turned off for the specific document
The proofing language is set incorrectly for the text being typed
The 'Hide spelling errors' option is enabled in Word settings
The paragraph or section has proofing exceptions applied
A corrupted custom dictionary file
The document is set to 'Do not check spelling or grammar' formatting
diagnostic_questions: Does this happen in all documents, or just one specific document?
What language is the text written in, and does it match Word's proofing language setting?
Have you checked if 'Hide spelling errors in this document' is turned on in Word Options?
Did this work correctly before in the same document, or has it never worked?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if spell check works correctly in a brand new, blank Word document
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This determines whether the problem is specific to one document or affects Word generally

troubleshooting_steps.action: If it works in a new document but not the current one, go to File > Options > Proofing and check that 'Hide spelling errors in this document only' is unchecked
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This specific setting can be accidentally turned on for individual documents, silently disabling spell check just for that file

troubleshooting_steps.action: Select all text in the document (Ctrl+A) and check the Language setting shown at the bottom of the Word window or under Review > Language
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If the proofing language does not match the actual language of the text, or is set to 'Do not check spelling or grammar', spell check will not function correctly

troubleshooting_steps.action: With all text selected, set the correct language and ensure the 'Do not check spelling or grammar' checkbox is unchecked
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly corrects the setting causing spell check to be skipped for that text

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check Word Options > Proofing to confirm 'Check spelling as you type' and 'Mark grammar errors as you type' are both enabled
troubleshooting_steps.reason: These global settings control whether Word actively checks text while typing across all documents

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the problem persists across all documents, try resetting or renaming the custom dictionary file
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A corrupted custom dictionary can sometimes interfere with the overall spell checking process

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run Office Quick Repair if spell check remains broken across all documents despite correct settings
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This can fix a deeper installation issue affecting the proofing tools

possible_solutions: Turn off 'Hide spelling errors in this document'
Correct the proofing language for the text
Uncheck 'Do not check spelling or grammar' for selected text
Enable 'Check spelling as you type' in Word Options
Reset a corrupted custom dictionary file
Run Office Quick Repair for persistent issues
prevention: Periodically check proofing language settings when working in multiple languages
Avoid accidentally toggling spelling and grammar options
Keep Office updated for proofing tool improvements

problem: Fonts are missing or displaying incorrectly in Word
description: A document opens in Word, but the text appears in a different font than intended, or Word shows a message that certain fonts used in the document are not installed on this computer.
symptoms: Text appears in an unexpected substitute font
Document layout looks different from how it was originally created
Missing font may be listed if checked in the font dropdown menu
Formatting looks inconsistent compared to the original file
possible_causes: The font used in the original document is not installed on this computer
The font file itself has become corrupted
A font was uninstalled or removed after the document was created
The document was created on a different computer or operating system with different available fonts
diagnostic_questions: Was this document created on this computer, or received from someone else?
Do you know the specific name of the font that should be used?
Does the document look correct when opened on a different computer?
Have any fonts been recently uninstalled or is this a newly set up computer?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if Word shows any message about a missing font when opening the document
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Word sometimes directly notifies the user which specific font is missing, saving time in diagnosis

troubleshooting_steps.action: Select the affected text and check the font name shown in the font box at the top of the screen
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms the exact font name the document expects, even if it is currently being substituted

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the Windows Fonts folder (Control Panel > Fonts) to see if the required font is installed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms whether the font truly needs to be installed, or if it exists but is not being applied correctly

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the font is missing, obtain and install it from a legitimate, licensed source, such as the font's official website or the organization that created the document
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Installing the correct font is the most direct way to restore the intended appearance of the document

troubleshooting_steps.action: After installing the font, close and reopen the document to confirm it now displays correctly
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Word needs to reload the document to apply a newly installed font

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the exact font cannot be obtained, ask the document's original creator to either embed the font in the file or provide a version using only commonly available fonts
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Embedding fonts when saving in Word ensures the document displays correctly on any computer, even without the font separately installed

troubleshooting_steps.action: For documents you create yourself, use File > Options > Save > Embed fonts in the file to prevent this problem for others in the future
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This proactively solves the missing font problem for anyone who later opens the document on a different computer

possible_solutions: Install the missing font from a legitimate source
Ask the document creator to embed fonts or use common fonts
Embed fonts when saving your own documents
Manually reapply the correct font if it becomes available
prevention: Embed fonts in important documents before sharing them
Use widely available standard fonts when possible for shared documents
Keep a record of custom fonts used in frequently shared templates

problem: Word file is marked as read-only and cannot be edited
description: The user opens a Word document and finds they cannot type or make any changes, with the title bar or a notification indicating the file is open in read-only mode.
symptoms: Title bar shows '[Read-Only]' next to the file name
Typing has no effect on the document content
A yellow bar may appear saying 'This file is locked for editing' or similar
Editing tools may appear greyed out
possible_causes: The file's read-only attribute is enabled in its file properties
Another user currently has the file open on a shared network location
The file was opened directly from a protected location, such as an email attachment preview or a website
The document itself has restricted editing enabled intentionally by its creator
Windows file permissions do not allow the current user to modify the file
diagnostic_questions: Where is this file stored, such as locally, on a USB drive, email attachment, or shared network drive?
Does the notification mention another person's name as currently editing the file?
Was this file intentionally protected by its creator, such as a form or template?
Have you tried saving a copy of the file to a different location?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if a yellow notification bar mentions another user currently editing the file
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If someone else has the file open on a shared location, Word opens it as read-only to prevent conflicting changes until they close it

troubleshooting_steps.action: If another user is editing it, wait for them to close the file, or contact them to coordinate access
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This resolves the issue naturally once the file is no longer locked by someone else

troubleshooting_steps.action: If opened from an email attachment or web browser, save the file to the computer first, then open that saved copy instead
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Files opened directly from email or browser preview modes are often automatically read-only until saved locally

troubleshooting_steps.action: Right-click the file in File Explorer, select Properties, and check if the Read-only checkbox at the bottom is selected
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This attribute can be set intentionally or accidentally and directly controls whether the file can be edited

troubleshooting_steps.action: Uncheck the Read-only checkbox in Properties if it is enabled, then click Apply
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly removes the restriction, allowing the file to be edited and saved normally

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check within Word under Review > Restrict Editing to see if the document itself has intentional editing restrictions set by its creator
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some documents are deliberately protected, such as forms, and may require a password from the creator to unlock full editing

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the file is on a network or shared drive, confirm the user account has proper write permissions to that location
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Insufficient permissions on a shared location will also cause files to open in a read-only or restricted state

possible_solutions: Wait for another user to close the shared file
Save the file locally before editing if opened from email or browser
Uncheck the Read-only attribute in file Properties
Enter the correct password to remove intentional document restrictions
Request proper write permissions for a shared network location
prevention: Save email or browser attachments locally before editing
Coordinate editing access on shared documents
Understand which documents are intentionally protected before assuming a fault

problem: Word crashes unexpectedly while working
description: While the user is actively typing, formatting, or performing an action in Word, the program suddenly closes completely without warning, potentially losing unsaved work.
symptoms: Word closes suddenly with no warning message
A Windows error report dialog may appear after the crash
Crash may happen during a specific action, such as inserting an image or using a certain feature
Unsaved changes may be lost unless AutoRecover captures them
possible_causes: A problematic add-in causing instability
A corrupted document triggering the crash
Outdated or corrupted graphics drivers affecting Word's rendering
A corrupted Office installation
Insufficient system memory for the current task
A specific feature or embedded object causing a known compatibility issue
diagnostic_questions: Does the crash happen during a specific action, such as inserting a picture, using a specific template, or printing?
Does this happen with all documents, or just one specific document?
Did this start after installing an add-in or a Windows/Office update?
When you reopen Word, does it offer to recover the document you were working on?

commands.purpose: Open Word in Safe Mode to test if it remains stable without add-ins and custom templates
commands.expected_result: Word runs without crashing in Safe Mode
commands.abnormal_result: Word still crashes even in Safe Mode, suggesting a deeper installation or file-specific problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: When reopening Word after a crash, allow it to recover the previous document if prompted
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This retrieves as much of the recent work as possible through the AutoRecover feature

troubleshooting_steps.action: Note exactly what action was being performed right before the crash happened
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A specific trigger, like inserting an image or using a particular feature, helps narrow down the exact cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test if the same crash happens in a brand new, blank document performing the same action
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This determines if the problem is with Word generally, or specific to the original document

problem: Excel workbook is corrupted and will not open properly
description: The user tries to open an Excel file, but receives an error message saying the file is corrupted or unreadable, or the workbook opens showing missing data, broken formulas, or strange formatting.
symptoms: Error message such as 'Excel cannot open the file because the file format or extension is not valid'
Message asking if Excel should try to repair the workbook
Workbook opens but shows missing sheets, data, or broken formulas
File will not open at all, showing a generic error
possible_causes: The file was not saved completely due to a crash or power loss
The file was copied or transferred incorrectly, causing data corruption
A virus or malware damaged the file
The storage device (USB drive, network drive) had an error while saving
The file extension does not match the actual file format
diagnostic_questions: Did the computer crash, lose power, or close unexpectedly while this workbook was open or being saved?
Where is the file stored, such as locally, on a USB drive, or a network location?
Was this file copied, emailed, or transferred from another location recently?
Do you have a recent backup or an earlier saved version of this workbook?

troubleshooting_steps.action: When Excel shows a recovery prompt, choose to let it try to repair the workbook
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Excel has a built-in repair feature that can often recover most of the data from a corrupted file automatically

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the automatic prompt does not appear, open Excel first, then use File > Open, select the file, and choose 'Open and Repair' from the dropdown next to the Open button
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This manually triggers the same repair process for files that do not prompt automatically

troubleshooting_steps.action: If repair fails, try the 'Extract Data' option within the same Open and Repair dialog, which attempts to recover just the values and formulas without full formatting
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This can recover the underlying data even when a full structural repair is not possible

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the AutoRecover folder for a recent automatically saved version of the workbook
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Excel periodically saves recovery copies that may be more recent or less damaged than the main corrupted file

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if a backup copy exists, such as in a cloud storage version history, a previous email attachment, or a USB backup
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A backup copy avoids the need for repair entirely and guarantees complete, undamaged content

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try opening the file on a different computer or using Excel Online to see if it opens differently
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the corruption is truly in the file itself, or related to a problem with this specific computer's Excel installation

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a malware scan if corruption happened without any clear explanation like a crash or transfer error
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Unexplained file corruption can sometimes be caused by malware damaging files on the system

possible_solutions: Use Excel's 'Open and Repair' feature
Use 'Extract Data' to recover values and formulas
Recover a version from the AutoRecover folder
Restore from a cloud or manual backup
Open the file on a different computer or in Excel Online to test
Remove malware if it may have caused the corruption
prevention: Save workbooks frequently while working
Use cloud storage with version history for important workbooks
Use a UPS to avoid power loss during saving
Safely eject USB drives before removing them
Keep antivirus software active and updated

problem: Formulas are not calculating in Excel
description: The user enters or expects a formula to calculate a result, but instead the cell shows the formula text itself, an outdated value, or does not update even after changing related data.
symptoms: Cell shows the formula text, like '=A1+B1', instead of the calculated result
Formula result does not update after changing the numbers it depends on
Only some cells update while others stay the same
Status bar at the bottom shows 'Calculate' instead of normal information
possible_causes: Calculation mode is set to Manual instead of Automatic
The cell is formatted as Text instead of General or Number, causing Excel to treat the formula as plain text
The formula contains a typing error preventing it from being recognized as a formula
Circular reference causing a calculation warning
The workbook is very large, causing intentional manual calculation to improve performance
diagnostic_questions: Does the cell show the formula text itself, like '=SUM(A1:A5)', or does it show a number that just seems wrong?
Does pressing F9 or manually recalculating update the values?
Is this happening with one specific cell, or all formulas in the workbook?
Was Calculation mode ever changed intentionally, such as for a large workbook?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the Formulas tab and look at the Calculation Options setting to see if it is set to Manual instead of Automatic
troubleshooting_steps.reason: In Manual mode, Excel only recalculates when specifically told to, which explains formulas appearing frozen or outdated

troubleshooting_steps.action: If set to Manual, change Calculation Options to Automatic
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This restores Excel's normal behavior of recalculating formulas immediately whenever related data changes

troubleshooting_steps.action: Press F9 to manually force a full recalculation and see if values update correctly
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms whether the underlying formulas are correct and just waiting for a trigger to recalculate

troubleshooting_steps.action: If a cell shows the formula text itself rather than a result, check if that cell is formatted as Text
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Excel treats text-formatted cells as literal text, displaying the formula instead of calculating it

troubleshooting_steps.action: Change the cell format to General or Number, then re-enter the formula (simply changing the format alone may not be enough; retyping or re-entering with Enter after changing format usually fixes it)
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This allows Excel to properly recognize and calculate the formula going forward

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for a circular reference warning at the bottom of the screen, which can prevent proper calculation of related formulas
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A circular reference, where a formula indirectly refers to its own cell, causes Excel to flag and potentially skip calculation

troubleshooting_steps.action: Carefully review the formula syntax for typing mistakes, such as missing parentheses or incorrect cell references
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A syntax error can cause Excel to treat the entry as plain text rather than a working formula

possible_solutions: Change Calculation Options from Manual to Automatic
Force recalculation using F9
Change cell formatting from Text to General or Number and re-enter the formula
Fix a circular reference causing calculation issues
Correct formula syntax errors
prevention: Keep Calculation mode set to Automatic unless intentionally using Manual for performance
Format cells correctly before entering formulas
Double check formula syntax when creating complex formulas
Watch for circular reference warnings and address them promptly

problem: Formula shows a #VALUE! error
description: Instead of showing a calculated result, a formula cell displays '#VALUE!', indicating that Excel cannot properly calculate the formula due to a problem with the type of data being used.
symptoms: Cell displays '#VALUE!' instead of a number
Error may appear after entering a new formula or after changing referenced cells
Related formulas that depend on this cell may also show errors
Small green triangle may appear in the corner of the cell with a warning
possible_causes: The formula is trying to perform a math operation on a cell containing text instead of a number
A referenced cell contains extra spaces or hidden characters that make it look like a number but is actually text
The formula references an empty cell where a number was expected in a way the function does not support
An array formula was entered incorrectly
A function is being used with the wrong type or number of arguments
diagnostic_questions: Which specific formula or cell is showing the #VALUE! error?
What cells does this formula reference, and what type of data do they contain?
Did this error appear after changing the data in a referenced cell?
Are any of the referenced cells possibly containing text that looks like a number, such as with extra spaces?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Click on the cell showing the error and check the exact formula being used
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms exactly what calculation is being attempted and which cells are involved

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check each cell referenced in the formula to confirm it contains the expected type of data, such as a number rather than text
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A #VALUE! error very commonly occurs when a formula expects a number but finds text instead

troubleshooting_steps.action: Look for cells that appear to contain numbers but are actually formatted or entered as text, often indicated by the number being aligned to the left instead of the right
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Numbers stored as text look correct visually but cause math operations to fail

troubleshooting_steps.action: Use the Excel error checking button that appears next to the cell (the small warning icon) and select 'Convert to Number' if offered
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly fixes numbers that are mistakenly stored as text

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for extra spaces in text or number cells using the TRIM function, or by carefully re-entering the value
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Hidden spaces can cause a cell to be treated as text even though it visually looks like a clean number

troubleshooting_steps.action: Break down a complex formula into smaller parts across separate helper cells to identify exactly which part of the formula is causing the error
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This isolates the specific portion of a complicated formula responsible for the #VALUE! error

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check that the correct number and type of arguments are being used for any functions in the formula, referring to Excel's built-in function help if needed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Using a function incorrectly, such as providing text where a number is required, directly causes this error

possible_solutions: Convert text-formatted numbers to actual numbers
Remove extra spaces or hidden characters from referenced cells
Correct the data type in cells referenced by the formula
Break down complex formulas to isolate the error source
Correct function arguments to match expected types
prevention: Keep consistent data types within columns used in calculations
Use data validation to prevent incorrect data entry
Double check formulas after copying them to new cells
Use TRIM and CLEAN functions when importing data from external sources

problem: Formula shows a #REF! error
description: A formula cell displays '#REF!', indicating that the formula is referring to a cell that no longer exists, usually because it was deleted.
symptoms: Cell displays '#REF!' instead of a calculated result
Error appeared right after deleting a row, column, or cell
Multiple formulas across the workbook may show this error at once if a widely referenced cell was deleted
Formula bar shows '#REF!' directly within the formula text where a reference used to be
possible_causes: A row, column, or cell that the formula referenced was deleted
A worksheet referenced by the formula was deleted or renamed
Copying and pasting a formula in a way that broke its intended references
An external workbook link was removed or the linked file was deleted or moved
diagnostic_questions: Did you recently delete a row, column, or cell in this or a related worksheet?
Does this error appear in one cell only, or in many cells across the workbook?
Was this formula referencing another worksheet or an external workbook?
Can you recall what the formula used to look like before the error appeared?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Click on the cell showing the #REF! error and look at the formula bar to see exactly where the broken reference is within the formula
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This shows precisely which part of the formula lost its reference, since '#REF!' will appear directly in place of the missing cell reference

troubleshooting_steps.action: Use Ctrl+Z to undo the recent action immediately if the deletion that caused this was just done
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Undoing the deletion is the fastest and most reliable way to restore the original references before they were broken

troubleshooting_steps.action: If undo is not possible, manually retype the formula with the correct, currently valid cell references
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly repairs the formula by pointing it to the correct, existing data

troubleshooting_steps.action: If many formulas across the workbook show this error at once, identify what widely referenced cell, row, or column was recently deleted
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A single deleted reference can cascade into many #REF! errors throughout a workbook if it was used in many formulas

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the formula references another worksheet that was deleted or renamed, correct the sheet name reference within the formula
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This restores the connection to the correct worksheet by name

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the formula links to an external workbook, check that the external file still exists at its expected location, and update the link if it was moved
troubleshooting_steps.reason: External links break if the source file has been deleted, renamed, or moved to a different folder

troubleshooting_steps.action: Going forward, before deleting rows or columns, check if any formulas depend on that data using Excel's 'Trace Dependents' feature
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps prevent future #REF! errors by showing what formulas rely on the data before it is removed

possible_solutions: Undo the recent deletion that caused the error
Manually correct the formula with valid cell references
Fix a broken worksheet name reference
Update a broken external workbook link
Use Trace Dependents before deleting data in the future
prevention: Check Trace Dependents before deleting rows, columns, or cells
Avoid deleting cells that other formulas rely on without checking first
Keep external linked files in consistent, stable locations
Be cautious when renaming worksheets that are referenced by formulas

problem: Formula shows a #DIV/0! error
description: A formula cell displays '#DIV/0!', indicating that the formula is trying to divide a number by zero or by an empty cell, which is not mathematically possible.
symptoms: Cell displays '#DIV/0!' instead of a calculated result
Error appears in calculations involving division, such as averages or percentages
Error may appear only for certain rows while others calculate correctly
Related formulas that depend on this cell may also show errors
possible_causes: The formula is dividing by a cell that contains a zero
The formula is dividing by a cell that is currently empty
A function like AVERAGE is being used on a range that is completely empty for that specific row
Data has not yet been entered for a calculation intended to be completed later
diagnostic_questions: Which specific cell is being used as the divisor (the number being divided by) in this formula?
Is that cell currently empty, or does it contain a zero?
Is this error expected until more data is entered, such as in an ongoing report?
Does this happen in one row only, or across many rows in the same column?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Click on the cell showing the #DIV/0! error and identify which part of the formula is the divisor
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This pinpoints exactly which cell is currently zero or empty, causing the division error

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if that divisor cell is genuinely supposed to have a value, and if data is simply missing, enter the correct value
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly resolves the error by providing valid data for the calculation

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the divisor being zero or empty is expected in certain situations, such as a report where data has not yet been entered for that row, wrap the formula in an IFERROR function
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This allows the formula to show a blank cell, zero, or a custom message instead of the error, keeping the report visually clean while the error is expected and harmless

troubleshooting_steps.action: For example, change a formula like '=A1/B1' to '=IFERROR(A1/B1,0)' or '=IFERROR(A1/B1,"")' depending on what should display instead of the error
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is the standard, recommended way to gracefully handle expected division errors in Excel

troubleshooting_steps.action: If using an AVERAGE function on a range that might be empty, consider using AVERAGEIF or checking with an IF statement first to avoid dividing by zero when no data exists
troubleshooting_steps.reason: AVERAGE internally divides by the count of numbers, and an entirely empty or non-numeric range causes this same type of error

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the error appears unexpectedly in a formula that previously worked, check if a value in the divisor cell was recently changed to zero or accidentally deleted
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps identify a recent change that introduced the error where it did not exist before

possible_solutions: Enter the correct, non-zero value in the divisor cell
Wrap the formula in IFERROR to handle expected division by zero gracefully
Use AVERAGEIF or an IF check to avoid averaging empty ranges
Correct a recently changed value that introduced the error
prevention: Use IFERROR proactively in formulas involving division where empty data is expected
Double check source data before performing division-based calculations
Use data validation to prevent accidental zero entries where not appropriate

problem: Macros are disabled and will not run
description: The user opens a workbook that contains macros, but sees a security warning saying macros have been disabled, and any buttons or automated features relying on macros do not work.
symptoms: Yellow security warning bar saying 'Macros have been disabled'
Buttons or automated tools in the workbook do nothing when clicked
Error message when trying to run a macro manually
Macro-enabled features work on some computers but not others
possible_causes: Excel's macro security settings are set to disable all macros by default
The file was downloaded from the internet and is marked as untrusted
The macro itself contains an error preventing it from running
The workbook is saved with a .xlsx extension instead of .xlsm, which does not support macros
Company security policies block macros entirely on managed computers
diagnostic_questions: Do you see a yellow security warning bar when opening the file, and if so, what does it say?
Where did this file come from, such as downloaded from the internet, received by email, or created locally?
Is this a personal computer, or a company-managed computer with possible security restrictions?
Do you trust the source of this file and its macros?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for a yellow security warning bar at the top of the workbook when it opens, and read exactly what it says
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is the most common and direct explanation, showing that Excel intentionally blocked the macros as a security precaution

troubleshooting_steps.action: If you trust the source of the file completely, click 'Enable Content' on the security warning bar
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is the standard, safe way to allow macros to run for a specific trusted file

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the file was downloaded from the internet, right-click the file in File Explorer, select Properties, and check the 'Unblock' checkbox at the bottom if present
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Windows marks internet-downloaded files as potentially unsafe, and unblocking removes this flag, allowing macros to run more smoothly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check Excel's Trust Center settings under File > Options > Trust Center > Trust Center Settings > Macro Settings
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This shows the current overall macro security level, which may be set to block all macros without any warning

troubleshooting_steps.action: Adjust the macro setting to 'Disable all macros with notification' if it is currently set to block them entirely, so you at least get the option to enable trusted macros going forward
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This provides a balance between security and functionality, showing a warning rather than silently blocking everything

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the file is saved with a .xlsm extension if it is genuinely meant to contain macros
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Standard .xlsx files do not support macros at all, and a file mistakenly saved in this format will lose any macro functionality

troubleshooting_steps.action: On a company-managed computer, contact the IT department if macros are needed for legitimate work purposes but are blocked by policy
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Company-wide macro restrictions are often intentional security measures that require IT approval to adjust

troubleshooting_steps.action: If a macro is enabled but still does not run correctly, check the macro's code in the Visual Basic Editor for errors, if you have the necessary permissions and knowledge
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The macro being allowed to run does not guarantee it is written correctly, and errors within its code can also prevent it from working

possible_solutions: Click 'Enable Content' on the security warning bar for trusted files
Unblock the file in its Properties if downloaded from the internet
Adjust Trust Center macro settings appropriately
Save the file with the correct .xlsm extension
Request IT approval for macros on a managed company computer
Fix errors within the macro's code if it still fails after being enabled
prevention: Only enable macros from trusted, known sources
Keep macro security settings at a reasonable, notification-based level
Save macro-containing workbooks with the correct .xlsm extension
Be cautious with macros in files received from unknown senders

problem: Pivot Table is not refreshing with updated data
description: The user updates the source data for a Pivot Table, expecting the Pivot Table to reflect the new numbers, but it continues to show old, outdated values until manually refreshed, or does not update even after refreshing.
symptoms: Pivot Table shows old data even after the source data has been changed
New rows added to the source data do not appear in the Pivot Table
Manually refreshing does not update the values
Pivot Table field list may be missing new columns added to the source data
possible_causes: The Pivot Table has simply not been manually refreshed yet, since this does not happen automatically by default
The Pivot Table's source data range does not include newly added rows or columns
The data source is set to a fixed range rather than a dynamic table
The Pivot Table is connected to an external data source that needs a separate refresh action
Filters applied to the Pivot Table are hiding the new data
diagnostic_questions: Have you tried right-clicking the Pivot Table and selecting Refresh?
Was new data added as new rows below the original data range, or within the existing range?
Is the source data a regular cell range, or was it converted into an official Excel Table?
Are there any filters currently applied to the Pivot Table that might be hiding the new data?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Right-click anywhere inside the Pivot Table and select Refresh, or use the Refresh button on the PivotTable Analyze tab
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Pivot Tables do not automatically update when source data changes, and a manual refresh is the first and simplest step

troubleshooting_steps.action: If refreshing does not show new rows that were added below the original data, check the Pivot Table's source data range under PivotTable Analyze > Change Data Source
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If new rows were added outside the originally defined range, the Pivot Table will not include them even after refreshing

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update the data source range to include the new rows and columns if the current range is too small
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly expands what the Pivot Table considers as its source data going forward

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consider converting the source data range into an official Excel Table using Ctrl+T before creating or updating the Pivot Table
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Excel Tables automatically expand to include new data added directly below or beside them, which then flows into the Pivot Table without manually adjusting the range each time

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if any filters are currently applied within the Pivot Table that might be hiding the new or updated data
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Data that does not match an active filter will not display, even though it is technically included in the underlying source

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the Pivot Table is connected to an external data source, such as another workbook or a database, use the specific 'Refresh All' option and confirm the connection settings are correct
troubleshooting_steps.reason: External data connections sometimes require a different refresh process than a simple internal data range

troubleshooting_steps.action: For workbooks where this happens frequently, consider enabling 'Refresh data when opening the file' under PivotTable options
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This ensures the Pivot Table automatically refreshes every time the workbook is opened, reducing the chance of viewing outdated data

possible_solutions: Manually refresh the Pivot Table
Expand the Pivot Table's source data range to include new data

description: The user clicks to start the slide show, either from the beginning or the current slide, but nothing happens, an error appears, or the presentation freezes before displaying the first slide.
symptoms: Clicking 'From Beginning' or 'From Current Slide' does nothing
Error message appears when trying to start the slide show
Screen goes black or shows a loading indicator that never completes
Slide show starts but immediately closes back to edit view
possible_causes: A problem with the display or projector connection settings
Presenter View settings conflicting with the available monitor setup
A corrupted or problematic embedded object on the first slide causing a failure
Outdated graphics drivers affecting slide show rendering
The presentation file itself has some corruption
Incorrect monitor selection settings when using an external display or projector
diagnostic_questions: Are you presenting using a single monitor, or with an additional monitor or projector connected?
Does any error message appear, or does the slide show simply not start at all?
Have you tried starting from a different slide, rather than always the first one?
Does this happen with all presentations, or just this specific one?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if an external monitor or projector is connected and confirm the display settings are correctly configured in Windows
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Incorrect display configuration is a very common cause of slide shows failing to start properly, especially in presentation settings with a projector

troubleshooting_steps.action: In PowerPoint, go to Slide Show > Set Up Slide Show and confirm the correct monitor is selected if using multiple displays
troubleshooting_steps.reason: PowerPoint needs to know which screen to use for the full slide show versus Presenter View, and an incorrect setting can prevent the show from starting as expected

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try starting the slide show from a slide other than the first one, to see if the issue is specific to the first slide's content
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps identify if a specific object or element on the first slide is causing the failure to start

troubleshooting_steps.action: If a specific slide seems to be the trigger, check that slide for a potentially corrupted embedded video, image, or object
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A single corrupted embedded object can sometimes prevent the entire slide show from starting or cause it to crash immediately

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update the computer's graphics driver, since slide show rendering, especially with multiple monitors, relies heavily on it
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Outdated graphics drivers are a common cause of display-related failures when starting a slide show

troubleshooting_steps.action: Turn off Presenter View temporarily under Slide Show settings and try starting the show again with just the basic full-screen mode
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This isolates whether the specific issue is with Presenter View's dual-screen functionality rather than the slide show itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run Office Quick Repair if the problem happens consistently across multiple different presentations
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This addresses potential underlying installation issues affecting the slide show engine specifically

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test the presentation and its slide show functionality well in advance of any important live presentation
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This allows time to resolve display and slide show startup issues before they become a problem in front of an audience

Fix or remove a corrupted embedded object on the problematic slide
Update the graphics driver
Temporarily disable Presenter View to isolate the issue

problem: Images are not displaying in a presentation
description: The user opens a presentation and finds that images which should appear on the slides are showing as blank boxes, red X icons, or are simply missing entirely.
symptoms: Blank white or grey boxes where images should be
A small red X icon in the corner of an empty image placeholder
Images that displayed correctly before are now missing
Problem appears only on certain computers, not the one where the presentation was created
possible_causes: Images were linked rather than embedded, and the linked image files have been moved or deleted
The presentation was transferred to a different computer without also transferring the linked image files
The image files themselves have become corrupted
A graphics driver issue affecting image rendering
Antivirus or security software blocking certain image file types from loading
diagnostic_questions: Were the images inserted using 'Insert Picture' and embedded directly, or linked from an external file location?
Is this presentation being viewed on the same computer where it was originally created, or a different one?
Did the images display correctly before, and if so, what changed recently?
Do all images show as missing, or just some specific ones?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if all images are missing, or just specific ones, to help narrow down whether this is a widespread or isolated problem
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A pattern affecting only certain images often points to those specific files being linked and broken, rather than a general presentation-wide issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Click on an empty image placeholder to see if any information appears about a missing linked file path
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This can directly reveal if the image was linked to an external file rather than embedded, and show where PowerPoint expects to find it

troubleshooting_steps.action: If images were linked, locate the original image files and either move them back to their expected location, or reinsert them directly into the presentation
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This restores the connection between the presentation and its image content, or permanently embeds the images to avoid the issue in the future

troubleshooting_steps.action: For future presentations that need to be shared or moved, always insert images so they are embedded directly, which is PowerPoint's default and standard behavior when using the normal Insert Picture option
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This prevents the entire class of problems related to broken links when a presentation is moved to a different computer or folder

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update the computer's graphics driver, since some display or rendering issues can prevent images from showing correctly even when the files themselves are intact
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This addresses a less common but still possible cause related to graphics rendering rather than missing files

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if antivirus or security software might be blocking or quarantining certain image file types, especially if the presentation was recently downloaded from the internet or an email attachment
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some security software can interfere with embedded or linked media in ways that cause images to fail to load

troubleshooting_steps.action: If specific image files appear corrupted, try replacing them with a fresh copy of the original image if available
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A corrupted individual image file cannot be repaired within PowerPoint and needs to be replaced with a working version

possible_solutions: Locate and restore missing linked image files
Re-embed images directly into the presentation
Update the graphics driver
Check antivirus settings for interference with media files
Replace corrupted individual image files with fresh copies
prevention: Always embed images rather than linking them when possible
Keep presentations and their linked files together if linking is used
Test presentations on the target computer before important events
Keep graphics drivers updated
